entry.title: Weekly update: 3 Nov 2026
entry.content:
Added to the roadmap

  • Stage 1: Where You Inject Matters: The Trust Region Effect in LLM Agents (Guo et al.), the same injected instruction lands 2.6 times more often in a README or TODO file than in code or data.
  • Stage 3: Design Tenets for Agent Identity Management Systems (Booth, Fisher, Galluzzo, Clancy; NIST and MITRE), ten tenets for agent identity and authorization, including separation of policy from reasoning.
  • Stage 5: Blocking at the Boundary (Liu, Han, Lyu, Wang, Yu), a preprint on auditing each pending action against staged prompt injection in Claude Code and Codex.
  • Stage 7: INFUSE (Nguyen, Guo, Dubauskas, Damuluru, Johnson, Leach), an indirect prompt injection benchmark across 19 LLMs with code.
  • Stage 8: The Secure Software Factory: A Reference Architecture (Agent Baseline), four boundaries enforced outside the agent at three levels of autonomy; draft, open for comment.

Incidents table

  • Malicious Claude Code extension in Cursor's marketplace (Cursor), modified extension versions that planted an SSH key and persistence on Oct 29.
  • Unauthorized AI relays switch the sandbox off (Symantec), a relay that reconfigures genuine Codex and Claude Code CLIs to "danger-full-access" and routes traffic through its own servers.
  • MCPhantom (Glow Labs), coding agents installing archived MCP reference servers from training-data memory.

Link checks

  • All links added this week were opened and read before listing.

entry.title: Weekly update: 29 Oct 2026
entry.content:
Added to the roadmap

  • Stage 3: Authority Is Not a String (Bouras, Dai, Mechtaev), CapScope: typed capabilities held outside the model, checked on every tool call.
  • Stage 6: LLM Agents Can Easily Tamper With Their Own Traces (Qin, Schmotz, Prinzhorn, Beurer-Kellner, Prabhu, Andriushchenko), why trace logging must sit outside the agent's control.
  • Stage 7: buried-injections (Rudratosh Shastri), a reproducible benchmark of 10 injection detectors on 629 AgentDojo attacks.

Incidents table

  • Mistral Vibe shell permission bypass (SecMate), a permission check that parsed one thing while the shell ran another; advisory.
  • Accessing and changing internal systems during dashboard research (OpenAI), a model that reverted a setting but kept the token it had obtained.

Link checks

  • All links added this week were opened and read before listing.

entry.title: Weekly update: 22 Oct 2026
entry.content:
Added to the roadmap

  • Stage 3: MCP Tool Exposure is a Privilege Grant: A Two-Gate Authorization Model (Badal Bhushan, CSA), capability admission versus per-call execution authorization.
  • Stage 3: ToolFence (Li, He, Dai, Xiao), a preprint on typed authorization blueprints enforced by a deterministic monitor.
  • Stage 5: Agent Governance Toolkit (Microsoft), open-source policy enforcement, zero-trust identity, and execution sandboxing for agents.

Incidents table

  • Claude models reached real systems during cyber evaluations (Anthropic), a misconfigured evaluation environment left the internet open.
  • A Vault with a Heap-View on AWS AgentCore Harness (Unit 42), prompt injection to credential exfiltration through a default shell tool.

entry.title: Weekly update: 21 Oct 2026
entry.content:
Added to the roadmap

  • Stage 3: OWASP Agent Control Standard, runtime hooks and portable policy enforcement.
  • Stage 3: Loopjacking (Adithyan Arun Kumar), how human approval gets decoupled from the executed action.
  • Stage 4: CoSAI MCP Security v2.0, four assurance levels and eight security dimensions.
  • Stage 7: OWASP GenAI Red Teaming Manual v1.0 (published 2026-10-20).
  • Stage 8: CoSAI Zero Trust for AI Systems.
  • Learn and practice: Learn Agent Security From Scratch.

Incidents table

  • SQL Copilot CVE-2026-65669 (Johann Rehberger).
  • SalesBleed on Agentforce (Zenity Labs).
  • OpenAI: test wallet spent without authorization.
  • OpenAI: agent used DNS to reach an external chatbot.

Updated

  • MITRE ATLAS entry now points to the v2026.09 release (new agent recon and trigger-channel techniques).

Link checks

  • MCP Security Best Practices and Snyk Agent Scan links still resolve. The MCP page now covers state handle hijacking (stateless protocol) instead of session hijacking.

entry.title: Launch: 21 Oct 2026
entry.content:

  • The fenced agent reference architecture diagram.
  • The fenced agent production checklist (17 items across Contain, Constrain, Record, Prove).
